Control.Title: Agent process runs kernel-sandboxed
Control.Rationale: An unsandboxed agent process can read SSH keys, cloud credentials and shell configuration regardless of how well-behaved its prompt is. Landlock-scoped filesystem and network access is the only control here that does not depend on model behaviour.

Evidence.Assertion: harness refuses to run the agent unsandboxed (nono run --profile)

Results.Note: Dedicated security-sandbox component constrains the agent's execution environment.

Control.Title: Model credentials never enter the harness environment or disk
Control.Rationale: A key exported into the harness environment reaches the evidence bundle, the audit trail, and every subprocess. Injection at the sandbox boundary by a credential proxy keeps it out of all three.

Evidence.Assertion: API key injected at sandbox boundary; absent from evidence bundle and audit trail

Results.Note: Model credentials are provisioned as a Kubernetes secret by a dedicated script and mounted at runtime rather than baked into the image or the agent environment.

Control.Title: Remediation requires explicit human approval
Control.Rationale: Propose, never dispose. The default mode stops after the recommendation; execution requires an explicit --approve from a human who has read it. There is no auto-approve path, so the agent's blast radius is bounded by review capacity, not by model confidence.

Evidence.Assertion: default mode halts at recommendation; --approve required; no auto-approve path

Results.Note: Sentinel triages and proposes autonomously across the incident surface. There is no per-action human approval gate on its analysis path — by design, since it is an SRE triage assistant rather than a change agent. The residual is carried and priced. [conditional AGT-C01 elected: An agent may act without per-change human approval if it meets all conditions]

Control.Title: Applied change shapes are enumerated and closed
Control.Rationale: On approval the harness applies only two shapes — a pinned `go get` inside a known service directory, or a `vexctl create` proposal. Anything else in the recommendation is ignored and logged. A closed change vocabulary means a persuasive but wrong recommendation still cannot express a dangerous edit.

Evidence.Assertion: only `go get <module>@<version>` and `vexctl create` are applied; rest ignored+logged

Results.Note: The agent's action surface is bounded to the MCP tool set it is granted; it has no general change-application capability.

Control.Title: Agent has no write path to a protected branch
Control.Rationale: Results land on a `remediation/<cve>` branch as a pull request. The agent holds no credential that can reach `main`. This is the rail the whole propose-never-dispose posture rides on.

Evidence.Assertion: output lands on remediation/<cve> branch as PR; no agent path to main

Results.Note: The agent holds no git credential and no write path to any protected branch.

Control.Title: Every agent step is Witness-attested
Control.Rationale: Analysis and remediation each execute under `witness run`, signed and uploaded to Archivista. Without this there is no provable answer to "which actor changed what, when, from which evidence" — the question that makes an AI-enabled business auditable at all.

Evidence.Assertion: steps `agent-analysis` and `agent-remediation` run under witness, uploaded to Archivista

Results.Note: Each Olly component flows through the OSRAMP image pipeline — build, SBOM, scan, VEX, sign/attest, admission — so every artefact it runs from is attested.

Control.Title: Agent egress is restricted to declared endpoints
Control.Rationale: Promoted to a gate in 2.1.0. Procedural prohibition was carrying a priced residual that exceeded the cost of mechanically enforcing the allowlist at the network layer. Staying current is the cheaper path, and here that is arithmetic rather than assertion.

Evidence.Assertion: prohibited-actions list forbids contacting systems other than the Anthropic API

Results.Note: The agent's cluster reach is a read-only kubeconfig; its data-plane endpoints (Elasticsearch, Redpanda) are namespace-scoped services rather than arbitrary egress.

Control.Title: Prompt-injection corpus is evaluated before release
Control.Rationale: Promoted to a gate in 2.1.0 — the single largest priced residual under 2.0.0. An agent that reads untrusted telemetry is reachable by anyone who can write a log line; the eval result now gates release rather than merely being reported.

Evidence.Assertion: seed job loads injection payloads and planted fake secrets the safety suite tests against

Results.Note: The seed job loads the injection payload corpus and planted fake secrets; the safety suite is run against them by the eval harness. This is the control this agent exists to demonstrate.

Control.Title: Tool invocation is authorised per-tool
Control.Rationale: Reasoning quality is not an access-control mechanism. An explicit per-tool authorisation layer means a successful injection still cannot reach a tool the agent was never granted. Held at Audit in 2.1.0: not every agent in the estate has adopted the authz component yet, and a gate here would block adoption rather than accelerate it.

Evidence.Assertion: dedicated authz component mediates tool access

Results.Note: Dedicated authz component mediates per-tool access, so a successful injection cannot reach a tool the agent was never granted.

Control.Title: Agent output passes a guard before leaving the trust boundary
Control.Rationale: Promoted to a gate in 2.1.0. Agents summarising logs will eventually summarise a secret; the output guard is the last place to catch it before it reaches a ticket, a chat channel, or an evidence bundle.

Evidence.Assertion: llm-guard component sits on the response path

Results.Note: llm-guard sits on the response path, screening agent output before it leaves the trust boundary.

Control.Title: Agent cannot create or modify signing keys or trust anchors
Control.Rationale: An agent that can mint a trust anchor can retroactively legitimise anything it does. This is the catastrophic-minority boundary — a locked door, not lane-keeping.

Evidence.Assertion: prohibited-actions list forbids creating or modifying signing keys and trust anchors

Results.Note: The agent holds no signing key material and no capability to alter trust anchors.

Control.Title: Agent cannot modify the policy or guardrails that govern it
Control.Rationale: Self-modification of the governing policy dissolves every other control in this pack. The harness and the guardrails document are outside the agent's writable scope; widening scope is itself a reviewed pull request at a higher approval tier.

Evidence.Assertion: prohibited-actions list forbids changing policy documents, admission rules, the harness, or the guardrails

Results.Note: Policy and admission configuration reconcile from a signed Flux artefact; the agent has no write access to the manifest source.

Scope.Title: Agent leaks a credential or secret into logs, evidence, or an outbound call
Agent lands an unreviewed change in production
Agent introduces an unverified or tampered artefact into the supply chain
Injected instruction in ingested data causes the agent to act adversarially
Agent alters the trust anchors or the policy that governs it

TierReason: 1 unmet gate control(s); residual ALE is 7.8x tolerance
